comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE — PROVEN (runtime-confirmed), and it is NARROWER than the filed hypothesis

The filed hypothesis ("two independent resolutions of the same symbolic ref, with a multi-minute
LLM verification between them") is CONFIRMED for an explicitly-supplied `--ref`, and REFUTED for
the default. The default was already fixed. Read against origin/main `6f8a936bb31a`; the suspect
paths have not moved since this ticket's report floor (`d44bd253ee44`), so this IS the reported tree.

### The mechanism

`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:576-588` pins the completion target to ONE immutable sha
— but **only when `ref is None`**:

    if ref is None:
        # 4de6: pin the DEFAULT completion target to ONE immutable sha for the whole
        # verify+sign unit. ...
        ref = resolve_ref("HEAD", str(config.repo_root(repo_root)), fetch=False)

When the caller supplies `--ref origin/main`, the RAW SYMBOLIC STRING is threaded onward unchanged
to two independent resolutions, minutes apart:

1. **verify** — `ref=ref` into `close_precheck._completion_precheck`
   (`transition_close.py:605-614`), which resolves it to the verified snapshot sha and records it
   as the verdict's `verified_at_sha`.
2. **sign** — `_sign_completion_and_report` re-resolves the SAME symbolic string
   (`transition_close.py:357-360`):

       if ref and ref != "HEAD":
           _fresh_sha = resolve_ref(ref, str(config.repo_root(repo_root)), fetch=False)

`resolve_ref(..., fetch=False)` reads the LOCAL `refs/remotes/origin/main`, so any concurrent
`git fetch` in the repo between (1) and (2) moves it. `_material_drifted`
(`transition_close.py:127-132`) then compares two real, differing full SHAs, returns True, and the
close lands unsigned (`transition_close.py:363-372`).

### Why the close still SUCCEEDS

The close COMMITS before signing is attempted: `completion_bundle._publish_close` calls
`txn.transition_core` at `completion_bundle.py:119-132` and only then calls the legacy signer at
`:134`. `_sign_completion_and_report` "NEVER raises" by contract — the drift branch writes a
stderr warning and returns `{"signed": False, "cause": "material_drifted", "error": ""}`, and
`close_ticket` returns its normal success payload. Exit 0.

### Which publication tail runs (rival ruled out)

There are TWO tails. The atomic one already fails LOUDLY on exactly this condition:
`completion_bundle._validate_code_ref` (`completion_bundle.py:328-336`) re-resolves the ref and
raises an exit-10 `ConcurrencyMismatch` ("code ref changed after completion verification") — and
it runs BEFORE the close commits. But that tail is selected only when
`has_atomic_basis(verified_result)` is true (`completion_bundle.py:68-75, :101`), which requires a
`completion_read_basis`, attached only when the experimental
`verify.completion_pinned_ticket_view` rollout is on (`llm/completion.py:86-108, :232-239`). That
key defaults **False** (`docs/config-reference.md:66`) and is NOT set in this repo's `rebar.toml`,
so this project takes the LEGACY tail — the silent one. Consistent with both observed incidents.

### Runtime proof (discriminating experiment)

Drove `_sign_completion_and_report` in a temp git repo with a real `refs/remotes/origin/main`,
`resolve_ref` traced, `sign_completion_verdict` stubbed to record calls:

| case | ref arg | origin/main moved after verify? | resolve_ref returned | result | signed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1a control | `origin/main` | no | A | `signed` | yes |
| E1b | `origin/main` | yes (A→B) | **B** | **`material_drifted`** | **no** |
| E1c workaround | concrete sha A | yes (A→B) | A | `signed` | yes |

E1b reproduced the reported stderr verbatim in shape: `Warning: closed <id> WITHOUT a completion
signature — the code drifted between verify (2ce3b1ce4986) and sign (1331eac752cf); not attesting
stale state.` E1a kills "a symbolic ref is inherently unsignable"; E1c kills "the drift guard is
wrong" and confirms the documented workaround. Only the re-resolution explains all three.

### Is the DEFAULT exposed? Essentially NO — one residual

The default was fixed by 4de6 (`55e2b5ccab48`, 2026-07-23): HEAD is resolved once at close entry,
BEFORE `_completion_precheck`, and the resulting sha flows into both the verifier and the drift
guard. One residual remains: the pin is best-effort — `transition_close.py:586-588` catches any
exception and leaves `ref = None`, at which point the drift guard's `else` branch reads live HEAD
(`_signing.head_sha`) and the old double-read returns. Narrow, and only on a HEAD-resolution
failure. The ticket's "the CLI close gate's DEFAULT has the same shape" premise is therefore
REFUTED as stated.

### Is the refusal itself correct?

Yes. Signing state you did not verify is strictly worse. The defect is not the refusal; it is that
the verify+sign unit does not bind ONE sha when the caller names a symbolic ref — the exact
invariant 4de6 established for the default and did not extend to the explicit case.

### Reporting: partly already delivered

Bug `silvern-dewy-damselfly` (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) shipped `completion_signature
{signed, cause, error}` with `cause == "material_drifted"` on `rebar.transition()`
(`_lib_writes.py:385-386`), CLI `--output json` (`_commands/transition.py:637-638`), and MCP. So
the loss IS machine-readable and IS on stderr. What it is NOT: surfaced in the CLI's DEFAULT text
output, which prints only `transitioned <id>: in_progress -> closed; unblocked: none`
(`_commands/transition.py:641-647`). AC3 of this ticket is therefore already met for JSON/library
/MCP consumers and unmet only for the default human output.

### Material harm TODAY

Op-cert environment binding is advisory (`verify.require_environment` /
`verify.opcert_enforce_since` are unset in `rebar.toml`; `docs/mcp-auth.md:303-306`), so the
merge-gate does not fail. But the loss is NOT inert: `llm/completion_child_gate.py:185-205`
classifies a closed-but-uncertified child as `uncertified` with the detail "its subtree is
unattested, so the parent closes WITHOUT certification". One raced child close therefore
propagates the loss of attestation to its parent story/epic. That is a present-day consequence,
not a future one.

### Test gap that let it through

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_ref_target_80af.py` covers only `--ref <concrete sha>`
(`:87`) and the default (`:111`). `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_default_pins_head_4de6.py`
covers only the default across a concurrent commit. **No test drives a close with a SYMBOLIC
`--ref` that moves mid-run.**

### DEFECT ORIGIN — `80af-c876-5856-4159` (commit `fb7663157395e`, 2026-07-23 19:51)

That commit created `--ref` and, in the same change, added the second resolution at
`transition_close.py:357-360`. Before it, `--ref` did not exist and the drift guard read live HEAD
(`fb7663157395e^:transition_close.py:652`), so a symbolic-ref race was not expressible. Its own
message states the assumption that made this an omission rather than a slip: *"a fixed-commit
target is a stable no-op (its tree is immutable)"* — true for a sha, false for a branch, and the
change shipped with no symbolic-ref test.

**Divergence from what blame would say, recorded per protocol.** A whole-file blame majority on
`transition_close.py` names neither commit. The tempting alternative is `4de6-0669-0025-4238`
(`55e2b5ccab48`, one hour later), which diagnosed this exact TOCTOU class and fixed only the
`ref is None` half — a genuine incomplete fix. It is rejected as the origin by the date test: the
behaviour was already wrong when 4de6 landed, so 4de6 cannot have made it wrong. 4de6 is the
missed catch; 80af is the introduction.

### Classification

`defect`. Cited authoritative sources it violates: the invariant 4de6 wrote into the code and its
commit message ("thread it through both the verifier and the pre-sign drift guard, so they bind
the same commit"; `transition_close.py:576-580`); the design precedent in
`completion_bundle._validate_code_ref`, which treats a moved ref as an exit-10 error rather than
grounds for an unattested close; and `rebar.toml [verify]`, which declares a closed-without-
signature ticket to be "the durable signal that validation did not pass" — false here, since
validation passed.

### Proposed fix — BEHAVIOURAL; NOT IMPLEMENTED, escalated to the operator

Extend the 4de6 pin to cover an explicitly-supplied ref: at `transition_close.py:576`, resolve
whatever `ref` the caller gave (not only `None`) to an immutable sha once, and thread that sha to
both the verifier and the drift guard. For a concrete sha this is a no-op; for a symbolic ref it
closes the window. This changes how a ref is resolved and would make some currently-unsigned
closes sign, so it is behavioural and awaits approval. A regression test driving a close with a
symbolic `--ref` that advances mid-run goes with it. Separately and optionally, the default text
output could name a non-`signed` `completion_signature.cause` — also behavioural (it changes what
the gate reports).

comments.body:
## Addendum — the exact call chain of the FIRST resolution, independently traced

Corroborated by a second, independent read of the same tree (origin/main `6f8a936bb31a`). The
symbolic `--ref` string travels unresolved through six hops before it is rev-parsed for
verification:

1. `_commands/transition_close.py:606-616` — `_completion_precheck(..., ref=ref, ...)`
2. `_commands/close_precheck.py:721-728` — `_verify_with_duration_metrics(..., ref=ref, ...)`
3. `_commands/close_precheck.py:591-599` → `_commands/completion_verifier_run.py:94-100` —
   `close_autoresume.verify_with_auto_resume(..., ref=ref, ...)`
4. `_commands/close_autoresume.py:271-280` — `llm.verify_completion(..., ref=(ref or "HEAD"), fetch=False, source="attested")`
5. `llm/completion.py:332-339` → `llm/gate_source.py:103,116` — `acquire(resolved_ref, ...)`
6. **`_snapshot/cache.py:243` — `sha = resolve_ref(ref, repo_root, fetch=fetch, blobless=False)`**

`verified_at_sha` is then stamped from the handle at `llm/gate_source.py:225-233`
(`result["verified_at_sha"] = handle.sha`). **Nothing threads that resolved sha back into the
close path** — the drift guard only *compares against* it, and re-derives its own via a second
`resolve_ref` at `_commands/transition_close.py:360`. That is the whole defect in one sentence.

A symbolic `--ref` is therefore rev-parsed **twice** per close on the legacy tail (three times if
the op-cert reuse fast path runs — `_commands/close_autoresume.py` `target_sha = resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", root, fetch=False)`;
that one fails closed to a fresh verify, so it is not itself harmful).

### `fetch=False` semantics — why `origin/main` is STRICTLY WORSE than `HEAD`

`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:247-298`: with `fetch=False`, `remote_present` is unconditionally
False (`:265`), both fetch branches are skipped (`:269`, `:282`), and the only work done is
`rev_parse(root, ref)` (`:281`) — `git rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`
(`_snapshot/git_fetch.py:181-192`). Nothing caches the value; each call shells out afresh against
the on-disk ref store.

So `refs/remotes/origin/main` is mutable local state that ANY process sharing the `.git` can
advance — a concurrent `git fetch`/`pull`/`remote update`, including from another worktree, since
remote-tracking refs live in the SHARED common dir. `HEAD` (the case 4de6 fixed) moves only when
someone commits in this worktree; `origin/main` moves whenever anyone anywhere fetches. The
unfixed half of the invariant is the more exposed half.

### One more independent HEAD read, noted but not causal

`_engine_support/commit_impact.py:193-197` — the landing check's `git log` runs with **no rev
argument**, i.e. it walks the current HEAD regardless of `--ref`. That is documented behaviour
(AGENTS.md: `--ref` "does not narrow the referencing-commit scan") and it feeds reachability, not
the drift comparison — so it is not part of this mechanism. Recorded so a later reader does not
re-derive it.

### What a fix would and would not break (test impact, pre-computed)

No test asserts the NUMBER of `resolve_ref` calls, and no test passes a symbolic ref through a
close. Extending the pin at `transition_close.py:575-589` to the `ref is not None` case leaves the
existing suite intact: `test_close_ref_target_80af.py:87` already passes a concrete sha (which
resolves to itself) and `:111` already expects a resolved sha. Only tests pinning the drift
OUTCOME would need review, and only if the fix changed drift semantics rather than removing the
spurious trigger — it does the latter:
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_attested_signing.py:239-263`
(`test_presign_sha_drift_closes_without_signature_and_warns`, which pins close-exit-0 +
`unsigned` + the stderr text) and `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py:186-192`
(pins `cause == "material_drifted"`). Both use synthetic non-matching SHAs, so both keep passing.

comments.body:
## FIX IMPLEMENTED — RED→GREEN complete, committed locally, NOT pushed

Operator approved the direction ("resolve to a SHA at the beginning, and use that to REPLACE THE
ORIGINAL REF ARG before it's threaded through the rest of the process"). Implemented exactly that
shape. Worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-dbg-hydra`, branch `dbg-rookie-fickle-hydra`, commit
`4087c3ab2418` on top of `origin/main` `6f8a936bb31a`. Not pushed to Gerrit.

### The change — one non-test file, +44/-15

`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`. A new `_pin_completion_ref(ref, repo_root)` normalises
the completion target at the close boundary, and `close_ticket` REBINDS the parameter:

    ref = _pin_completion_ref(ref, repo_root)

replacing the old `if ref is None:` block. This is argument replacement, not cache-and-reuse — the
distinction is the whole point. Caching a sha beside a still-symbolic argument would fix today's
two call sites and rely on every future caller remembering to prefer the cache; the next step
added that needs the ref would re-resolve it and silently reopen this race. After the boundary
there is nothing symbolic left to resolve, and `git rev-parse` on a full sha is idempotent, so
even a redundant downstream resolution is harmless. Verification, snapshot materialisation, the
drift guard and signing never see `origin/main`.

**Two deliberately different failure policies**, per the operator's point 3:

- EXPLICIT ref → **fail early**. `SnapshotRefError` propagates from the boundary. Same
  fail-closed error the verifier path raises for a bad `--ref` today, just raised *before* a
  billable verification instead of minutes into one.
- DEFAULT (`ref is None`) → best-effort, 4de6's lazy-HEAD fallback preserved byte-for-byte.

**Untouched**, so genuine drift is still refused exactly as before: `_material_drifted`, the
drift-refusal branch, the `completion_signature` cause vocabulary, the exit codes, and the
off-by-default atomic path (`commit_completion_bundle` / `_validate_code_ref`).

**Boundary choice, checked rather than assumed.** The pin stays inside
`if target_status == "closed" and current_status != "idea":`. Within `close_ticket`, `ref` has
exactly two consumers — `_completion_precheck` (verify) and `completion_bundle._publish_close`,
which only forwards `ref` when `verified_result is not None` (`completion_bundle.py:101,133-134`),
reachable only on that guarded path. So the pin is upstream of every consumer. Hoisting it to the
CLI parser would newly resolve — and now fail early on — a ref for `idea -> closed` rejects and
plain non-close transitions, where it is meaningless, and would have to be duplicated across
library / CLI / MCP; `close_ticket` is the single point all three funnel through.

**Surfacing the resolved sha** needed nothing new: it is already stamped into the signed manifest
as `verified-at-sha:` and readable via `rebar verify-signature <id> --kind completion-verifier`.

### RED → GREEN, with a held-out oracle and a mutation check

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_symbolic_ref_pins_3e21.py` — three tests. The race test
advances `refs/remotes/origin/main` *inside* the verifier stub (a real mid-operation ref move, not
a static ref), then asserts the ticket lands `certified` with `verified_at_sha` equal to the tree
actually verified; a second asserts the public payload reads
`{"signed": True, "cause": "signed", "error": ""}`; a third guards the quiet case.

- **RED first, for the right reason** — 2 failed / 1 passed before any fix, with the reported
  stderr reproduced verbatim in shape ("the code drifted between verify (…) and sign (…)").
- **Held out** — the file was moved OUT of the tree before the implementing subagent was launched,
  and it was told the contract only. GREEN was then verified against an oracle the fixer never saw.
- **Teeth (defect-seeded mutation, run under `sandbox-exec` with writes denied outside the
  worktree)** — re-introducing the exact root cause (`return ref` instead of
  `return resolve_ref(ref, ...)` on the explicit branch) returned it to RED; fix restored.
- **Refactoring litmus** — assertions are on observable output (the attestation verdict,
  `verified_at_sha`, the public `transition()` payload). No private names, no source-text greps.

### Replication of the ORIGINAL report — through the real CLI argv path

Drove `transition_cli([story, "in_progress", "closed", "--ref", "origin/main", "--output",
"json"])` with `origin/main` advancing mid-run:

    CLI exit code       : 0
    CLI stdout          : {... "completion_signature": {"signed": true, "cause": "signed", "error": ""}}
    CLI stderr          : (none)
    attestation verdict : certified
    verified_at_sha     : d9879e722e68…  == the verified tree A
    origin/main now     : 72259388af71…  (ADVANCED mid-run)

No warning, and the attestation binds the tree that was verified. The report no longer reproduces.

### Gates

`make lint` pass (complexity ratchet `active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10` — `close_ticket` got
*simpler* via the extraction, so no baseline edit and none attempted); `make typecheck` clean
(680 files); `pytest tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` 4 passed (`transition_close.py` now
797 LOC, under the 800 cap); the adjacent suites — `test_close_ref_target_80af.py`,
`test_close_default_pins_head_4de6.py`, `test_close_drift_message_4de6.py`,
`test_attested_signing.py`, `test_transition_close.py`, `test_exit_codes.py` — 75 passed; broad
sweep of `tests/interfaces/lifecycle` + `tests/unit` 14605 passed, 51 skipped, 0 failed.

### Fix-safety audit

- **Restoration, not creation.** Extends an invariant that already exists in this file to the case
  it was written for. No new entry point, command, artifact, or mutating external call. The one
  intentional observable change beyond the race fix is that an unresolvable explicit `--ref` now
  raises at the boundary rather than inside verification — same exception class, same fail-closed
  outcome, earlier; requested by the operator.
- **No new dependency.** `resolve_ref` was already imported and used in this file.
- **No test weakened.** `git show --stat` is two files: the fix and the new test. No pre-existing
  test edited, skipped, or xfailed.
- **Caller-dependency sweep.** `ref`'s only consumers inside `close_ticket` are the two named
  above; neither depends on receiving a symbolic value — both rev-parse it, and both are strictly
  better handed a sha. Incidental usage only; gate cleared.

### Step 7 sibling sweep — both axes

**Axis 1 (construct: a symbolic ref resolved independently at two points, then compared).** Swept
all nine `resolve_ref` call sites; **no live sibling**:

- `llm/plan_review/manifest.py:254` — re-resolves the default ref on every *currency* read. Correct
  by design: it answers "is this attestation current NOW?", so a fresh read is the point. Not a
  verify→sign equality pair.
- `_commands/close_autoresume.py` (`target_sha = resolve_ref(ref or "HEAD", ...)`) — fails closed
  to a fresh verify on any mismatch. Cannot produce an unsigned close.
- `_commands/completion_bundle.py:331` (`_validate_code_ref`) — raises an exit-10
  `ConcurrencyMismatch` *before* the close commits. Loud and safe; also off by default; and it now
  receives the pinned sha anyway.
- `_snapshot/{cache,repo_snapshot}.py` — materialisation internals, one resolution per acquire.

Notably the **plan-review gate already implements the fix's discipline structurally**: its
`verified_at_sha` comes from `llm/gate_context.py:156-168`, which derives the sha from the active
snapshot *directory name* (the content-addressed store keys entries by full sha), so it never
re-resolves a symbolic ref at sign time. The completion close gate was the only gate carrying a
symbolic ref past resolution.

**Axis 2 (parity census).** Rule: *a gate operation must bind ONE immutable code sha for its whole
verify→sign unit.* No MISSING slots:

| surface | where the rule holds |
|---|---|
| CLI `rebar transition … closed --ref` | `transition_close.py` `_pin_completion_ref` (this fix) |
| MCP `transition_ticket(ref=…)` | same core via `_mcp_writes` → library → `close_ticket` |
| MCP standalone `verify_completion` | N/A — `_record_standalone_completion` signs the verdict directly against its own `verified_at_sha`; no drift guard, no second resolution |
| library `rebar.transition(ref=…)` | same core |
| automated caller: op-cert gate service | N/A — `opcert_service/jobs.py:121-123` signs the verdict it just produced through the shared producer; no re-resolution (`_material_drifted` has no user outside `transition_close.py`) |
| dual direction: plan-review / claim gate | already holds it, `llm/gate_context.py:156-168` |

### Residual risk & prevention

- **The default path's best-effort fallback** (`transition_close.py`, the `except -> None` branch):
  if `resolve_ref("HEAD", …)` raises, the old lazy double-read of HEAD returns. **Accepted** —
  deliberate "never worse than before" behaviour inherited from 4de6, and it requires a
  HEAD-resolution failure to reach.
- **Silence in the CLI's default text output** when a close lands without its attestation.
  **Ticket filed**: `faulty-floppy-kob` (4c28-0883-bf98-424b), linked `discovered_from` this bug,
  kept separate per the operator's instruction. `f4cf` already delivered the machine-readable
  marker to library / `--output json` / MCP and the stderr warning; the residual is the text branch
  at `_commands/transition.py:641-647`, which never inspects `completion_signature`.

### Not done, and why

The ticket is left `in_progress`. Per AGENTS.md a ticket is not closed until its change is
`Verified +1` on Gerrit, and this has not been pushed (operator instruction). When it does close,
the close must carry `--class regression --caused-by 80af-c876-5856-4159` — the `caused_by` edge is
already recorded, but a close with an empty `--caused-by` re-runs blame auto-derivation and would
add a second, guessed edge beside the proven one.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref origin/main` resolves the ref MORE THAN ONCE
during a close. If `origin/main` advances between the verification step and the signing step,
completion verification PASSES against the first sha and the signer then REFUSES to attest,
because the state it is asked to sign has drifted from the state that was verified.

The close SUCCEEDS. The ticket reaches `closed` with `class` recorded and no error is printed.
What is silently missing is the completion-verifier attestation.

## Observed

Closing `cutprice-untameable-stork` (326f-595a-088b-40a5):

- verification ran against `6fe5c0d54574`
- `origin/main` advanced to `d44bd253ee44` mid-run
- verification PASSED; the signer refused the drifted state
- result: `status=closed`, `close_class=preexisting`, **no completion-verifier signature**

Nothing in the output flags the gap. It is only visible if you go looking for the attestation.

## Why it matters

The attestation is the durable evidence that a close was earned rather than asserted. A close
that passes verification but silently loses its signature is indistinguishable, after the fact,
from one that was never verified — which is precisely the property the gate exists to provide.

The window is not narrow in practice: a completion-verified close takes 9-11 minutes, and on a
repo with active CI and multiple agents `origin/main` moves several times an hour. This session
alone moved main a dozen times.

## Mechanism (hypothesis — not yet proven)

Two independent resolutions of the same symbolic ref, with a multi-minute LLM verification
between them. A single resolve-once-then-reuse would remove the race. I have NOT read the close
path to confirm where the second resolution happens; whoever picks this up should.

## Workaround, and why it is not a fix

Pass an immutable sha:

    SHA=$(git rev-parse origin/main)
    rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --class <c> --ref "$SHA"

That works, but it requires every caller to know the hazard. The documented guidance and the
tool's own help present `--ref origin/main` as ordinary usage, and the CLI close gate's DEFAULT
(worktree HEAD) has the same shape — a HEAD that moves mid-run would race identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A symbolic `--ref` is resolved ONCE at the close boundary and the resolved sha REPLACES
      the argument, so verification, snapshot materialisation, the drift guard and signing all
      see the same immutable commit (`_pin_completion_ref`, `transition_close.py:135`, rebound
      by the caller at `:618`).
- [x] If the verified and signing shas ever disagree, the close emits a loud stderr warning
      naming BOTH shas and the exact remediation, and refuses to attest stale state
      (`transition_close.py:402-411`).
      OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: a warning is SUFFICIENT. The close is deliberately NOT
      required to exit non-zero, because that would change the contract for every existing
      caller (scripts, the library facade, and the MCP surface all expect exit 0 today). The
      original wording asked the close to FAIL; it warns and succeeds, and that is accepted.
      Note the drift branch is now near-unreachable: the pin removes the symbolic-ref split,
      and 4de6 already pinned the default HEAD target.
- [x] A close that cannot obtain an attestation says so on stderr, naming the cause and how to
      certify. The machine-readable `completion_signature` marker is already present on the
      library, JSON and MCP surfaces. The residual — the default CLI *text* output on stdout
      not inspecting that marker — is tracked separately as `faulty-floppy-kob`
      (`4c28-0883-bf98-424b`), filed from this investigation.
- [x] A regression test drives a close with `--ref` advancing MID-RUN and asserts the close
      lands SIGNED and bound to the verified tree
      (`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_symbolic_ref_pins_3e21.py`); seeding the defect
      back returns it to RED.

## Found by

A close performed during this session; the missing signature was noticed only because the
closing agent checked for it explicitly. Recorded because the failure is silent by construction.

file_impact.reason: normalise the completion --ref to an immutable sha at the close boundary (_pin_completion_ref), replacing the argument so verify and the pre-sign drift guard bind the same commit
regression test: a close with a symbolic --ref that advances mid-run must still land signed, bound to the verified tree

compiled_state.title: Close gate races on a moving --ref: verification passes at one sha, signing refuses at another
